answer.because: For exact inputs x = 1 - 10^-n, head's acos (pi/2 - asin(x)) loses most of its digits to cancellation: at precision 20 with x = 1-1e-20 it returns 1.414213562373079e-10 (relative error 1e-14), and with x = 1-1e-60 it returns 9.99999984e-17 when the true value is 1.414e-30 (off by about 14 orders of magnitude), while base matches a high-precision 2*asin(sqrt((1-x)/2)) reference to full precision.
